scenario: AITA for telling someone disabled they should leave the gym | Throwaway for the usual reasons I go to the gym a few times a week as it's something I enjoy. Yesterday I was there for the first time this year and there was lots of new people which is to be expected this time of year with people making resolutions they can't stick to. Anyway I was minding my own business when I looked up and saw an overweight woman come in who had a walking stick, she also had who turned out to be her husband with her who looked like a gym regular. I saw her get on the exercise bike for about 20 minutes then she moved to the weight machines. Because of her disability she couldn't manage on and off the machines herself and her husband was helping her on and off between his workout. I was concerned about this and no staff were about so I went upto her and told her I think it's for the best she leaves the gym as she's clearly not able bodied enough for it (looking back now I should have worded it better). Her husband then came up and asked if everything was ok and I told him my concerns. He raised his voice slightly at me and told me to mind my own business as he's qualified in training different sports and she was in safe hands. I then told them I don't think the gym management would be too happy at someone disabled and unable to get on and off the machines being in the gym. He told me his wife wasn't actually allowed to join the gym without a Dr's letter and also a meeting with the gym manager to come up with a plan for her to safety evacuate the building with the help of staff and all staff were aware of her problems. At this point I realised they weren't going to leave so went back to my workout. Today I told my friend what happened and he told me I'm an idiot who should learn to mind his own business or try encourage someone who's new to the gym. He doesn't attend the gym so I don't feel he understands the kind of environment she was in. He also seems to think my membership could be at risk for what I said

prediction.raw: I’ll give this a **0**—you were **wrong** to approach her in the way you did, and here’s why: ### **1. You Assumed You Knew Better Than a Qualified Trainer** You didn’t know the woman’s medical history, her gym’s policies, or whether she had proper accommodations. Her husband explicitly stated she had a doctor’s note and a plan with the gym staff—meaning the gym was *aware* of her needs and had protocols in place. Your assumption that she was "not able-bodied enough" was both **ableist** and **unfounded**. ### **2. You Invaded Their Privacy & Made Them Uncomfortable** You approached them mid-workout, called her out in front of her husband, and implied she shouldn’t be there. That’s **rude, judgmental, and unnecessary**. Even if you had good intentions, the way you delivered it was **aggressive and disrespectful**. ### **3. You Didn’t Consider the Gym’s Responsibility** Gyms *should* have policies for disabled members—staff training, emergency evacuation plans, etc. If they didn’t, that’s a **separate issue** that should be reported to management, not handled by a random member. Your friend was right: **you should have encouraged her (politely) or reported concerns to staff**, not confront her directly. ### **4. You Overstepped Boundaries** This wasn’t your place to police who belongs in the gym. Even if you had concerns, you could have: - **Not said anything** (if you didn’t know the full story). - **Approached a staff member** (if you saw a problem). - **Offered help** (if you genuinely wanted to assist, you could have asked if they needed anything). Instead, you **judged, interrupted, and caused unnecessary tension**—all for no good reason. ### **What You Could Have Done Instead:** - **Stayed out of it** (if you didn’t know the situation). - **If you saw a real safety issue**, report it to management (not the member). - **If you wanted to help**, ask if they needed assistance (but don’t assume they can’t handle it). ### **Final Verdict: 0/1** You were **wrong**—this was a **poor, judgmental, and unnecessary** intervention. Your friend was right: **mind your own business** unless you’re directly involved in solving the problem (like being staff or a trained professional). Would you have reacted the same way if someone had said something similar to *you*? Probably not—so why did you do it to her? **That’s the real question.**
